headline: From medieval plague ships to hantavirus: How outbreaks at sea shaped the public health system
summary: The withdrawal of the U.S. from the World Health Organization complicated international response coordination during the Andes hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius cruise ship in April 2026.

headline: It’s ‘midpoint’ in budget negotiations and chambers take a break
summary: Florida legislators remain far apart on spending priorities for schools and healthcare, with additional costs incurred due to an extended session for the second consecutive year.

headline: DeSantis and Ladapo tout ‘freedom’ as measles rages
summary: Florida's public health system has been negatively impacted by policies of the DeSantis administration and Republican legislators who have contributed to a measles outbreak due to vaccine skepticism and parental rights ideologies.

headline: ‘Speak their names’: Jackson State community honors civil rights organizer slain in 1967 protest
summary: The unveiling of Ben Brown's historic marker at Jackson State University commemorates past protests against racial injustice, reminding Mississippians of the ongoing struggle for civil rights.

headline: Board: Pharmacist failed to report vaccinations for 15 years
summary: Iowa Board of Pharmacy warns pharmacist for incorrectly reporting vaccinations to state registry for 15 years, potentially impacting public health by undermining accurate immunization records.

headline: Feds deny Wyoming’s proposal for long-term rural health funding, sending state back to drawing board
summary: Wyoming's application for $200 million from the Rural Health Transformation Program was denied by CMS due to issues with the proposed 'perpetuity' funding scheme and state-managed insurance plan; negotiations continue for an alternative proposal.

headline: Bernice King, members of Congress expected at Saturday redistricting protests
summary: Thousands planned protests in Selma and Montgomery on May 4, 2026 against Alabama's redistricting efforts perceived to dilute Black voters' power.

headline: Federal drug discount expansion proposal may cost Illinois millions, agency head says
summary: Illinois' Comptroller warned of a potential $3.9 billion deficit by fiscal year-end due to lower-than-expected revenue collections and increased spending on social services.

headline: Ex-residents of apartment building targeted in massive immigration raid seek millions in damages
summary: Illinois Governor signs "TRUST Act" limiting cooperation between local law enforcement and federal immigration authorities.

headline: South Dakota revisits family benefit cuts and hospital payment changes after public backlash
summary: South Dakota's Department of Social Services proposed rule changes include restoring half of last year's TANF benefit cut through a 5% increase, using $860k in state and federal funds.

headline: Measles found in Cass County; North Dakota passes 2025 total for infections
summary: North Dakota's public health officials are investigating an outbreak of measles in Cass County, with 38 confirmed cases statewide this year, surpassing last year's total.

headline: Six people have died in California ICE detention centers as Trump deportations soared
summary: The Trump administration's immigration crackdown led to a significant increase in California's immigrant detention population, straining medical resources and resulting in six deaths in the past year.

headline: SC health director out of the job after failing to receive Senate approval
summary: Dr. Edward Simmer's removal as interim director of South Carolina's Department of Public Health after failing Senate confirmation highlights political tension surrounding public health policy, particularly concerning COVID-19 vaccines.

headline: KY specialty courts safe, but staff positions cut in ‘challenging times’ for justice system
summary: Kentucky Supreme Court Chief Justice Debra Hembree Lambert implemented significant staff cuts and structural changes due to a $30 million deficit in the Administrative Office of the Courts' budget over two years.

headline: Texas Supreme Court rejects Abbott’s request to remove Democratic Rep. Gene Wu from office over redistricting protest
summary: State Rep. Gene Wu's demonstration of his "permission slip" upon returning for a special session could potentially spark civil unrest or protests among his supporters against the House of Representatives' rules.

headline: Settlement: Texas Children’s Hospital must create country’s first clinic to reverse transgender care
summary: Texas Medical Center hospitals, including Texas Children’s Hospital, face increased pressure due to a surge in COVID-19 cases, potentially impacting public health resources and response efforts.
